transcript: Hey, I'm going to tidy up a bit. Do you mind if I move some of your stuff around?
Oh, um sure... Just be careful with the photo albums
No worries, babe. I'll treat them like they're my own.
Okay, just... Just let me know if you need help identifying what goes where.
Sure thing. How about we listen to some soft music while doing it?
Music would be great. Can we play the folk playlist on Spotify?
I knew you'd suggest that. But hey, I love it too.
Thanks, Ben. Sorry, I can be a bit protective of my things sometimes.
That's alright. We all have our quirks, right? I'll get started.
Let me know if you find my missing knitting needle, okay?
You lost another one? How on earth do you manage that?
It's a mystery. Even Sherlock Holmes wouldn't solve.
Well, in that case, let the hunt begin.
I appreciate you, you know? For dealing with my idiosyncrasies.
Gwen, that's what makes you, you. And I wouldn't have it any other way.
Hey, there's something I've been meaning to talk about...
Oh? What's up?
Well, it's about my past. Something I've kept hidden, but I feel it's time you knew.
Alright, I'm here to listen.
Before we met, I was in another relationship and... I have a child from that time.
Wait, you have another child?
Yes, a son. He stays with his mom mostly, and I've been trying to be more involved in his life.
And why haven't I heard about this before?
I was scared. Scared about how you'd react, about how it might change things between us.
That's... a lot to take in.
I know, I should have told you sooner. But I didn't know how.
I appreciate you being honest with me, but I need some time to think about all this.
I understand, take your time. I hope you know that I still care about you and nothing's gonna change that.
I know, Leo. Thanks for your honesty. Just... give me some time, yeah?
Of course, take as much time as you need.
Dad, where are all these boxes for?
Just sorting out some old stuff.
Looks like quite a job. Do you need help?
No, I've got this, thanks.
You know, I've been thinking about getting my own place...
Really? And leave me to my rare plants?
Well, they seem to like you more than me anyway.
That's nonsense! You're always welcome to stay, you know?
I know, Dad. Thanks.
As long as you're not moving just because of these boxes.
Dad, it's not about the boxes.
I know, honey. It's just... you're growing up too fast.
Aren't I supposed to?
You are, it's right, but... you know...
Yeah, I know, Dad. It's okay.
You ever worry about not being accepted, Esme?
Accepted by whom?
By anyone, I suppose.
I don't have the luxury of worrying about acceptance, Finn. I have a job to do.
Hm, maybe that's the difference between us...
You think so?
Yeah... I often worry about what people think of my past.
But it's in the past, Finn. We learn from it, we move on.
Not always that easy, little sister.
Life isn't easy, Finn.
Guess the lighthouse does get lonely sometimes.
Well, at least you've got your paintings to keep you company.
They don't talk back much. Anyway, I've said too much.
It's alright, Finn. Everyone has fears, even me.
Really? I imagine your fears are much different than mine.
Hey, Isabelle. Can we talk about something?
Of course, Gwen. What's up?
You know, it seems like we spend a lot of time together...
Yeah, we do. You're a great friend.
I was thinking... maybe we could, you know, be a bit closer.
What do you mean by 'closer', Gwen?
I Well... like, physically? Maybe a hug every now and then...
Oh, I see. You want a more touchy relationship.
Yeah, I guess that's it.
I have to think about it. Hugging isn't something I normally do.
Yeah, I understand. Take your time.
But Gwen, just so you know, this won't change anything between us, right?
Absolutely. I just thought it might be nice to hug sometimes, but only if you're comfortable with it.
I appreciate your honesty, Gwen. I'll think about it.
That's all I could ask for, Isabelle. Thanks.
You know, Jas, maybe we should just... take a quiet moment together?
Just like... not talk for a bit?
Yeah. Like, just sit together and... let things settle. You know?
Can't deny, that sounds appealing. But, is this like a magic thing?
What? No. Why would you think that? It's just...normal people stuff.
Alright, just checking. You've been acting a little... different lately.
Different how?
Like... distracted maybe? I don't know, Belle. I can't quite put my finger on it.
No, it's nothing like that. I'm just...it's just me being me.
Okay... if you say so.
So... quiet time?
Yep... quiet time...
Great, just... you and me here.
Yeah, just us... let's see how this goes.
Good... I think we need this.
It’s a weird time, isn't it?
Yeah, everything feels so... uncertain.
We're in this together, you know.
I know, and I appreciate it. It's just that... I keep thinking, you know?
I understand, sweetie. I've been there myself, it's hard.
It's not just about me, though. It's larger than that.
Yes, and that's okay. Those feelings don't have to be all-consuming.
It feels like it sometimes.
I get that. But remember this: Holding space for others doesn’t mean losing yourself.
That's true. Thank you, Gwen.
Anytime, Benjamin. Even amidst all this, remember, we are in this together.
Yeah, we are. Somehow, that feels a bit comforting.
And it should, love. Let's just take things one day at a time, alright?
Yeah, one day at a time. That seems manageable.
That's the spirit, darling. And don't forget, you're never alone in this. Okay?
I see you've been cleaning up the living room.
Yeah, thought we could use a bit of tidying up.
It's appreciated, but you could've let me know. I don't want you doing all the work.
It's not a big deal, really. Besides, you're usually busy with your research.
Still, I don't like the idea of you thinking you have to do it all by yourself.
It's just cleaning, Imelda, not some heroic task.
Nonetheless, we live together. It's a shared space and therefore a shared responsibility.
Well, you can take the lead next time. For now, I don't mind.
Alright, fair enough.
Now, how about we enjoy our newly cleaned living room?
Sounds like a plan. Anything particular you feel like doing?
Cup of tea and a chat?
I'd like that.
Honey, I've been thinking about something...
Yeah, what's up, Mom?
I've decided to take some steps this year to achieve a personal goal of mine.
Sounds intriguing, Mom. What's it about?
Well, I am thinking of learning Portuguese. Always found it an interesting language and culture!
That's pretty cool, Mom. But isn't it going to be hard with your work?
Yes, no doubt. But I've always believed that you should at least try to do the things you love.
I can't disagree with that. I'm secretly learning magic, remember?
That's right! Exactly the same principle!
Do you have any plans about how you're going to learn it?
I've enrolled in an online course. It's going to be a mix of video lectures and practicing with others.
That sounds like a great plan, Mom.
I hope so. I'm nervous but excited.
Just like how I felt when I started learning magic. It's never easy at the start, but if it's something you love, I'm sure you'll do great.
Thanks, my love. Your support means a lot.
Hey, check this silly one out: Why don't scientists trust atoms?
Hmm, not sure, Ethan. Why?
Because they make up everything!
Oh, that’s quite funny—given I actually deal with atoms, or well, particles even smaller than that!
I knew you'd get a kick out of that one!
Let me guess, another result of your late-night documentary marathons?
Got it in one!
Your repertoire of science jokes could give a stand-up comedian a run for their money.
Maybe I should consider a career change?
From a software developer to a comedian? Risky, but I'd buy a ticket to your show.
Ha! Think I'll stick with my day job for now, but thanks for the vote of confidence.
Keep honing your skills, Ethan. You never know when a career change might come in handy.
Always the planner, huh?
That's how I've always been.
Well, don't ever change, Imelda. Your analytical mind is your superpower.
Hey Naomi, how was the coding boot camp today?
Oh, it was interesting. We had a heated discussion on whether to use Java or Python for a project.
And you chose...?
Python. Its simplicity and versatility won me over. But I still appreciate the Java supporters' opinions.
That's great, Naomi. It's good to see that you respect their choice, even if you disagree.
Well, it’s important to value each opinion. They made good points too.
Exactly, every opinion and choice made, brings something new to the table.
Yeah, totally. By the way, how's your daughter doing?
She's doing great, keeps me on my toes though with her curiosity.
I can imagine. She must ask a lot of questions?
Yeah, she does. I might not always have the answers, but I still let her know her questions are important.
That'll help her become a creative thinker, Leo. Your approach is admirable, even if it differs from what I've seen so far in parenting.
Thank you, Naomi. Appreciation brings out the best in people, don't you agree?
Absolutely, Leo. And it builds bridges between differences too. It's been a long day, I'll catch up with you later.
Sounds good, Naomi. Have a great evening.
Gwen, do you think it's a good idea to move this couch nearer to the window? Plenty of sunlight will be a bonus, right?
That could brighten up the room, Oliver. But maybe we'd risk the fabric fading over time.
I hadn't thought of that. You've got a point there, Gwen. How about this bookshelf? Should we leave it here?
Maybe we could move it a few inches to the left? It may balance the room’s authentic charm better.
Fine, just a few inches to the left it goes then.
And these throw pillows...aren't they a bit too dull for the sofa?
Dull or not, they match really well with the rug's color, don't you think?
Well, yeah, now that you mention it, they do blend in quite nicely.
How about your cats? Won’t our tidying up disturb them too much?
I guess you're right. They can be really finicky about their space.
Let's call it a day then. We can continue tomorrow. This is enough for now, isn’t it?
Yeah, you're right. We've done quite well today. Thanks, Oliver.
Hey, sis. How about we take a quiet moment together? Just to let things settle?
Yeah, sure. I could use a break. What's on your mind?
I think I've been so tied up recently with work...sometimes I overlook things. Family stuff, you know?
Well, that's natural. You're loaded with responsibilities... insanely stacked work schedule, fatherhood.
Right, but I just want to make sure that I'm not missing out on anything big. Especially between you and me.
That's sweet of you. But isn't that what big brothers do? Ensuring the kid sister's not troubled?
True, it comes with the title. I feel like things change, even without us realizing it.
Well, that's how life is. Nothing remains constant, not even relationships.
Yeah, it's still a bit unsettling. But we'll manage, we always did.
We sure have, haven't we? But you do need to pace things out, Leo. Take it one step at a time.
Maybe you're right. I’ve got too much on my plate lately.
It's okay. Just remember, you don’t have to do it all at once. I’m here and we’ve got each other’s backs.
Yeah, thanks Naomi.
Of course, bro. Now, let's go grab some ice cream.
So, I've been thinking about that new project, Amara...
Which one? The environmental art piece?
Yeah, that one. I just... I don't know. I'm not sure it's the right message.
Hmmmm, and why's that?
Well, I mean, it's beautiful and all, but isn't it a little preachy?
Are you saying I should tone it down?
Maybe? I don't know...
Cal, you've always been sincere about your thoughts. I deeply appreciate that about you.
Yeah, but it's YOUR project, not mine...
But it's your opinion I wanted. We might not always agree, but I value your perspective.
Well, alright then. As long as you're sure...
Oh, I am. Even if we don't see eye to eye, I value your opinion and who you are as an individual.
Well, thanks Ama. Appreciate that.
Of course, Cal. You know, our differences make us stronger.
Yeah, I guess they do, don't they?
Hey, look at this.
What's that?
I noticed this tiny caterpillar on the leaf. Its patterns look kinda cool.
Hmm, they are pretty detailed for something so small.
Yeah, it's fascinating. It's these small things, you know?
What do you mean?
Just that we get so caught up in the big picture, we forget the details... they're important too.
That's deep, coming from you.
Uh, yeah. Just something I thought about.
I'll keep that in mind.
Please do. It could bring some change.
Some change, huh?
Yeah, some change. Who knows?
Alright. I'll think about it. Thanks for sharing.
No problem. It was just a thought.
And then, I said to him, \"That's not how Kuramitsu builds his towers!\"
You really tell it like it is, don't you?
I guess it comes with the job, huh?
Maybe so...
Speaking of, there's something I've been wanting to talk to you about...
What is it, Oli?
Lately, well...I feel like maybe we could be closer. You know, physically.
Oh... um.
I'm not pressuring you, sweetie, just... it's something I've been thinking about.
Give me some time to think about it, alright?
Of course, take all the time you need.
Thanks, Oli. I appreciate it.
Anytime, babe.
There's this particular spot where I see the sun rise every morning, you should check it out someday.
Really, grandpa? I’d love it. I was just thinking to sketch a sunrise for my next project.
I might not have your artistic eye, but the way the light dances on the water... it's worth the early wake-up.
I can imagine it. Light scattered across the water like shimmering eyelashes.
Eyelashes? I never thought of it that way.
Yeah, the unexpected beauty in things, you know?
I see it in you. Constantly learning, growing.
That’s sweet of you to say, grandpa.
It's important to look for the small things, the overlooked beauties.
Like the lashes of morning light you were talking about?
Exactly. Like them.
You're right, grandpa. I’ll get up early tomorrow to see them myself.
Good. It’ll make my sunrise coffee even more special, knowing you are appreciating the same view.
I'm looking forward to it, grandpa. Can’t wait to experience it.
And I can't wait to see your interpretation of it in your sketch.
Mom, do you think I should come over tonight?
Well, honey, it's entirely up to you.
It's just... I don't know. I've got a lot on my plate.
You don't have to push yourself, sweetie. Do what feels right.
But I feel like I've been avoiding you. That's not fair.
Isabelle, we all have our moments. You have yours, and it's okay.
Are you sure, mom?
Of course I am. You should do what makes you comfortable.
I'll think about it, okay?
That sounds perfect, sweetie. Just remember, no pressure.
Hey, Finnegan.
Oh hi, Noah. How was your day?
Pretty eventful, I'd say. I've something to tell you.
Go ahead, I'm listening.
You know how I usually spend my evenings, right?
Sure, you're usually at the pool.
Actually, not always... You know what they say about all work and no play, right?
That's kind of unexpected. What have you been up to then?
I've been doing some stand-up comedy. People seem to like it...a lot.
Stand-up comedy? You?
Yes, surprising I know, but everyone needs a little laughter, don't you think?
Of course, we all do. But this is a complete change of direction for you.
Funny isn't it? Who would have thought?
Well, all the best, Noah. Always good to try new things, isn't it?
Thanks, Finnegan. I appreciate it. It was hard to tell you, though.
Ever think about what really matters to you, Noah?
That's deep, Finn. What exactly do you mean?
Just...you know, what drives you? Day in, day out.
Well, there's family. My swimmers. Comedy, on good nights. Everything else is just...extra, I guess.
Comedy, huh? That's a surprise.
Part of the fun, isn't it? Keeping guessing. You?
Solitude. Sea. Paint brush. That's enough for me.
That does sound peaceful. But don't you ever feel lonely?
Can't say I do. Lonely and alone are different things, my friend.
I can see that. Being surrounded by people doesn't always mean you're not lonely.
Right, it's not the volume, is it? It's the depth.
Never really thought about it that way...
Try it sometime. Makes the world look a bit different.
Alright, Finn. Thanks for the perspective.
Anytime, Noah. That's what friends are for.
You know, despite our differences, I appreciate your perspective, Gwen.
Oh, yeah?
Yeah. We may not agree on everything, but you have your reasons. I respect that.
Well, respect is mutual, Benjamin.
Although, I'm a bit curious. How did you decide on social work?
Hmm... I guess it was about making a difference, you know? Like you with your environmental work.
Yeah. No impact is too small, right?
Exactly, it's all about giving a damn and trying to create some positive changes.
And I think that's what makes you such an amazing social worker, Gwen.
That goes for you too, Benjamin. Your passion for the environment is contagious.
Thanks, Gwen. Let's continue making a difference in our own ways.
Definitely! Let's do our best.
Hey, was thinking of cooking dinner tonight.
Oh, yeah? What're you in the mood for?
Thought I could make some of that saffron risotto you like.
Now you are talking. That sounds nice.
Great, just need to grab some stuff from the greenhouse.
Wait, greenhouse? Since when do we have a greenhouse?
Um, well, have been tinkering a bit out back...
And you didn't think to mention it?
Was sorta surprisin' you with it.
Geez, you're full of surprises.
So, you in for the risotto?
Yeah, sure. Let's do it.
Perfect, will get started then.
Wait, can I maybe help out?
I'd like that. Let's do this together.
You wouldn't believe what happened today.
Oh, really? What's up?
You know Jennifer and Samantha at my office, right?
Yeah, vaguely. What about them?
They had a disagreement...about that Foster care project.
That doesn't sound like them. They always seemed to work well together.
That's what I thought too, but today was... different.
Things must have gotten heated.
It got really intense. I don't know, I feel so drained.
I can see that. It's always hard when people around you are in conflict.
Yes, It's just...I have this weird gut feeling about it.
It's alright. Just remember, it's their disagreement to solve.
I know, it's just hard to stand by and watch, you know.
I understand. But I'm here with you, okay?
Yeah...thanks, love.
Izzy, should I come over to your place?
Right now?
Yeah, I just finished a design and I want to show you.
Uh…Sure, but my place is a mess.
I don't mind, sweetheart.
Well, I mind. I wasn't expecting company.
Hmm, it’s not like I haven’t seen your place messy before.
That's different. It's… more messy than usual.
Is it? What have you been up to?
Just... stuff.
Cool. I don’t need to come up. I can just wait for you downstairs.
Maybe that's best.
Alright, see you in a bit then?
Yeah, see you soon, Cal.
You know, babe, I really appreciate having you in my life.
That's sweet of you, Jax. Out of nowhere, huh?
Yeah, just reflecting a bit I guess.
Well, I appreciate you too. You bring stability to my chaotic life.
Well, I do try.
Try more often, won't you?
Now, that's something to ponder on.
Tomorrow you'll forget the 'pondering' part.
Not really. I might surprise you.
Oh, should I be on the look out for surprises then?
Maybe, maybe not.
You're just impossible, aren't you?
Comes with the package, babe.
Well, I appreciate that package nonetheless.
And I, yours.
Hey babe, just saw your basement.
Oh...you did?
Yeah, full with injured animals. It's a mini zoo down there.
I... I can explain.
No need, babe. Your love for animals... it's amazing.
You're not upset?
Nah. Well, a heads-up would've been nice, I guess.
Well, I didn't think you'd be okay with it...
Isabella, I love you. And part of that is loving your kindness towards all living things.
And you're okay with sharing our home with them?
Maybe not 'okay'. But I'm willing to compromise.
I appreciate that, Sophia.
Just make sure our bed doesn't turn into a shelter for injured raccoons alright?
I promise, our bedroom is a no-raccoon zone.
Good. That's all I ask for.
So I've been thinking...
Yeah?
I mean, about the stuff you said last time. About magic and everything.
Oh, that. Right...
I just want you to know, I might not fully understand it, but... I'm trying.
I appreciate that, really.
It's just not something I've been exposed to, you know?
I get it. It's not exactly common.
But just because it's different doesn't make it wrong, right?
Exactly. It's just... another way of looking at the world.
Like yoga is for me, I guess.
Exactly. They might look different from the outside, but they're not that different at heart.
Looks like I've got some learning to do, huh?
We all do, all the time.
I really appreciate your patience, Bell. Thank you.
Hey sweetie, you've been pretty ensconced in your books recently. What is it that you've been diving into?
Oh, just studying some different things, dad. Bit of this and that, you know.
Your eyes tell a different story. There's a spark there. There's something more, isn't it?
You sure know how to read people. Well, it's not entirely academic... I'm studying magic.
Magic, huh. I never took you for an illusionist fan.
It's not illusionist magic. It's more of... the arcane variety.
Huh, I see. And what does that mean for your future?
That's the thing... I don't know. It's a path less traveled, for sure.
Are you worried?
Yes, and no. I mean, it's risky and uncertain, but it feels right. You know, like an adventure?
I see. You know, whatever you decide, just remember that it's your journey. And I'm here if you need me.
Thanks, dad. That means a lot to me.
Anytime, kiddo. Now, let's get some dinner, shall we?
You know, sometimes I find myself missing the good old days.
How so?
Well, like when we used to gather in my backyard tree house. Those were simpler times.
Yeah, time flies, right? There's a certain charm to those memories.
Indeed. The laughter, the innocent banter. Wish I could go back in time.
But we've also grown a lot since then, don't you think?
Yeah, we have. But at times, I still yearn for those carefree days.
It's okay to miss someone or something, it shows how much we cared about it.
Yeah, you're right, Mia. It's the relationships and experiences that define us.
We must learn to treasure the past but also move forward, right?
Absolutely. But, it's easier said than done.
True, and it's a process. Take your time, Oliver.
Thanks, Mia. I appreciate it.
Anytime, Oliver. We are friends after all.
Indeed we are, Mia. Thanks for always being there.
Can you lend me a hand here, dear? This mess won't sort itself out.
Can I finish this article first? I've been meaning to read it all week.
Take your time, I can manage.
Have you found the corkscrew?
Not yet, but I unearthed some old recipes that we could try.
Ah, that sounds like you found distraction rather than the corkscrew.
Well, you're not entirely wrong.
How about we clean everything up right after dinner?
Sounds fair, you are on dishes?
As long as you're doing the cooking, yes.
Well then, prepare yourself for another culinary adventure.
As long as it's one of your 'real' recipes and not a 'found' one.
You'll never know if you don't try it, love...
Well, we'll find out tonight, won't we?
Yes, indeed we will, Ethan.
Hey, I see you visited the hospital again today.
Yeah, took Jaxon for a routine check-up. It was nothing serious.
Okay, got it. Just worried about you carrying all that around, you know.
I'm fine, Oli. I have a life outside my son.
It's not just about Jaxon, Mia. It's that...that painting stuff!
What do you mean?
I found your painting supplies tucked away. Mia, why would you hide something like that?
You were snooping around my stuff?
No... but I wonder why you don't share your talent. Do you think I wouldn't understand?
It's not that, Oliver. It's just... I don't know...
Is it because you think I'd judge you?
Maybe... I just want to be more than a mum and a nurse in everyone's eyes.
And you are, Mia. We all have layers. Like my greenhouse...
You have a greenhouse?
See? Even I have secrets... We should all learn to value every piece of ourselves more. And share, when we're ready.
I've been thinking about what you were saying the other day...
Oh? And which part was that?
About putting myself in others' shoes more. You know – understanding where they’re coming from.
Ah, yes. Feeling empathetic can broaden your perspective significantly.
But isn't that... subjective? Interfering with objectivity?
I wouldn't necessarily say that. It's not losing objectivity, it's gaining empathy. They're not mutually exclusive.
Empathy. That's a tough one for me.
But you're not incapable of it.
Yeah, I guess you're right. It's just...different for me.
That's alright. You don't have to adopt my ways. It’s all about understanding.
Although, I could try...you know, seeing things from your perspective.
Well, that sounds encouraging! But remember, don't force it. It's an invitation, not an imposition.
Invitation, not an imposition. Got it.
Glad to hear that.
You really are something, aren't you?
Oh, hey Gwen, don't you think the place is a bit messy?
Really? I thought it was just a little untidy, not too bad.
Yeah, but I'd feel better if we straighten up a bit.
OK, sure. I don't mind.
Great. How about I start from this side, and you take the other?
Fine with me. But let's not throw away anything without confirming with each other. Some stuff might look like junk, but it could be important.
Yeah, totally. I agree with you there.
Let's just get this over with.
Well, that's the spirit, isn't it?
You could say that, yes.
Alright, let's get to it then!
Yeah, let's do this.
And we could turn up some music while at it, what do you say?
Sure, as long as it's not too loud.
Deal!
Son, there's been a disagreement among your uncles about the wine for our monthly tasting.
Oh? That seems unusual. What's the issue, Dad?
Your uncle James thinks we should shop locally, while uncle Tom insists on the tradition of supplying wines from abroad.
Hmm, both arguments make sense.
Indeed. But their bickering is disrupting our quiet evenings. What's your take?
Well, why not do both? They can each bring their preferred wines and may the best selection win.
That seems fair, but you know your uncles, they're stubborn.
Seems like this is more about the argument itself than the wine.
Could be... they've been stepping on each other's toes lately.
Be that as it may, we should focus on what these nights are about – good company, fun, and tasting wines.
You're right, these disputes are trivial.
Just remind them of that, Dad. We don't need to solve their differences, they're adults.
They could learn from your maturity, son.
Well, we can't all be wizards in the kitchen pretending to resolve disputes, can we?
Ah, you've got a point there, son. I have my ways, don't I?
Ethan, you seem somewhat reserved today.
Yeah, I guess I am. I got a few things on my mind.
Is it something you want to talk about? I'm here if you ever need an ear.
Well, not sure if it would interest you...but, there's this situation with my team at work.
Disagreement over a project?
In a way, yes. We're split over which direction to take our new software. Both sides have strong arguments.
Remember, consensus isn't always a sign of a good decision. Sometimes, it signifies a lack of scrutiny.
Yeah, I know. I’ve been all analytical about it, but making a decision isn't easy.
Well, that’s part of leadership, Ethan. Tough choices, unpopular decisions. Not always fun, is it?
No, definitely not. Reminds me of your research predicaments, right?
Absolutely. Disagreements are part and parcel of life. It's how you navigate them that counts.
True that. Thanks, Imelda. Your perspective always helps.
Anytime, Ethan. Remember, you’re the best judge here.
I'll keep that in mind.
That's the spirit. Now, how about a quick cello session to lighten the mood?
You know, Amara, it's strange but I've never shared this with anyone before...
What is it, Gwen?
I, um...I had a child when I was 16. I gave them up for adoption.
Oh, Gwen, I had no idea...
It’s something I've kept buried for a long time. It's difficult, you know?
Absolutely, Gwen..., such decisions... they're tough.
Yes, and it's a whole part of my life that just feels... lost.
I can only imagine... You're incredibly brave, Gwen.
I'm not sure about brave. Sometimes I feel like I'm still that terrified 16-year-old girl.
Yeah, you're right.
